{"self_assessment": "Impact: I chose the animal and the design. I proposed a fish with a big body and a round tail because its outline reads clearly to a judge who doesn't know our plan. I sketched it on the pad at the start as three strokes: top body line, belly, and a tail branching off where the body lines meet. That gave the table a buildable plan from minute one. The standing result is a recognizable fish, with about 108 of 111 dominoes connected to the start.

Execution: I designed the sketch around how dominoes fall, with rounded curves, gentle branches, and a single start that carries every line. I made repeated close inspections of the nose and the middle crossing, and from them I confirmed that the fall carries through the whole body and tail. I stood one fallen domino back up. I also chose to leave the middle crossing alone once it checked out, so we didn't risk bumping it.

Collaboration: I assigned the three strokes to Omar, Hana and Jack at the start, so everyone had a job right away and no one waited. I kept updates short and clear, and I stayed off the nose joint so we didn't bump each other's hands. I asked everyone to keep hands off the finished middle and nose before the push.

Leadership: I set the direction in the first minute, divided the work, and kept the table coordinated through the build. I made the call to stop adding and let the fish stand. The table finished with a clear, connected picture and no last-minute risk.", "my_share_percent": 30}
